knowledge_list_resources.name: knowledge_list_resources
knowledge_list_resources.description:
List all reference documents and structured data exposed as MCP resources by
this CloverDX Server, along with their URI, name, description, and MIME type.
Resources are static files from the CloverDX knowledge library installed on
the server (distinct from the searchable `knowledge_base_search` entries).

Use this to discover available reference URIs before calling `knowledge_read_resource`.
Typical content includes graph XML reference, CTL language reference, and
component configuration guides published as MCP resources.

resources.description: List of available MCP resource URIs with their metadata.

mimeType.description: MIME type of the resource content.

description.description: Short description of the resource content.

knowledge_base_read.name: knowledge_base_read
knowledge_base_read.description:
Read the full content of a specific knowledge base entry by name. Content is fetched
fresh from the library on every call (no caching) so in-place edits to the .md file
on the server are visible immediately.
The `name` parameter is required. Use `knowledge_base_search` to discover available
entries — it returns a JSON list with name, description, tags, and lane per entry.
The `name` parameter accepts either a bare kebab id (e.g. 'csv-file') or a
'cdx:scope/id' pointer used in skill authoring (e.g. 'cdx:component/csv-file',
'cdx:guide/data-app', 'cdx:graph/atomic-write-rename'). Supported scopes:
component, graph, ctl, jobflow, guide, troubleshooting.

name.description: Name of the knowledge entry. Accepts kebab id ('csv-file') or 'cdx:scope/id' pointer ('cdx:component/csv-file', 'cdx:guide/data-app').

component_list.name: component_list
component_list.description:
Browse and discover available CloverDX component types.
Use this to identify which component to use when the correct type is not yet known.
Returns a compact list: type key, display name, category, and short description.

After finding the right type, call `component_get_info` (step 2) to get the full
configuration details — ports, parameters, and default metadata — before adding
the component to a graph.

Filter by category to narrow the search:
- readers: components that read data from files, databases, streams, APIs
- writers: components that write data to files, databases, streams, APIs
- transformers: single-input components that transform, filter, or split records
- joiners: multi-input components that join, merge, or combine record streams
- jobControl: components used in jobflows (run graph, loop, switch, etc.)
- others: lookup joins, sequence generators, and data generators

The searchString filter splits on whitespace into tokens; every token must appear
(case-insensitive, literal substring) in at least one of the type, name, category,
shortDescription, or description fields. All tokens must match (AND logic).
Example: 'join data' matches DBJOIN (name contains 'Join', shortDescription
contains 'data').

searchString.description: Optional whitespace-tokenised filter. Every token must appear (case-insensitive, literal substring) in at least one of type, name, category, shortDescription, or description. Tokens AND across the component.

sandbox_analyze_file.name: sandbox_analyze_file
sandbox_analyze_file.description:
Analyse or decode a binary/structured file in a sandbox. Required: action, sandboxCode, sandboxPath.

Choose the action by file type:
• PDF (.pdf)                         → action=extract_pdf
• Excel (.xlsx / .xls / .xlsm)       → action=extract_excel
• CSV / delimited (.csv / .tsv / ...) → action=profile_csv  ← USE THIS to understand a CSV file
• Any other text file (.txt, .md, .json, .xml, .grf, source code, …) → use `sandbox_read_file` instead

Action details:
• extract_pdf   — Extracts readable text from a PDF document. Supported: .pdf only. Optional: pages (e.g. '1-5' or '3', 1-indexed; defaults to whole document).
• extract_excel — Returns tabular content from an Excel file. Default: first 50 data rows of the first sheet + sheet list. Optional: sheet (name or 0-based index), rows (data-row range, e.g. '1-50'), include_sheet_list (boolean). Refuses files larger than 50 MB.
• profile_csv   — Profiles a CSV/delimited file for data-quality insights: detected delimiter, row count, and per-column stats (inferred type, null rate, distinct count, example values). Character encoding is auto-detected (handles non-UTF-8 files such as ISO-8859-2); pass encoding to override. Optional: delimiter (auto-detected if omitted), encoding (auto-detected if omitted), max_rows_scanned (default 10000), distinct_sample_size (default 5).

distinct_sample_size.description: action=profile_csv only. Number of example distinct values to emit per column. Default 5.

rows.description: action=extract_excel only. Optional data-row range to return, 1-indexed over data rows (excludes header). Examples: '1-50' (default), '1-20', '50'. Multi-range specs are not supported.

include_sheet_list.description: action=extract_excel only. Whether to prepend the full sheet list above the active sheet's content. Defaults to true when 'sheet' is omitted, false otherwise.

sandboxPath.description: Full file path within the sandbox (e.g. 'data-in/report.pdf').

max_rows_scanned.description: action=profile_csv only. Max data rows to scan for type inference / null rate / distinct counts. Default 10000.

delimiter.description: action=profile_csv only. Optional delimiter character. Accepts ',', ';', '|', actual tab, or '\t'. Omit to auto-detect from the first line.

sheet.description: action=extract_excel only. Optional sheet name (e.g. 'Customers') or 0-based index ('0', '1'). Defaults to the first sheet.

encoding.description: action=profile_csv only. Optional character encoding (e.g. 'ISO-8859-2', 'windows-1250'). Omit to auto-detect (handles non-UTF-8 files); pass 'detect' to force detection.

pages.description: action=extract_pdf only. Optional page range to extract (1-indexed, inclusive). Examples: '3' for a single page, '1-5' for a range. Defaults to the whole document.

sandbox_delete_directory.name: sandbox_delete_directory
sandbox_delete_directory.description: Delete a directory from a CloverDX sandbox. Use with caution — this is irreversible and may remove nested content.

component_get_info.name: component_get_info
component_get_info.description:
Resolve a CloverDX component by type or name (case-insensitive). Returns plain text, not JSON.
If exactly one match is found, returns full formatted details: usage guidance,
input/output ports incl. propagated metadata, and properties incl. required/conditional groups.
If multiple matches are found, returns a compact candidate table — re-query with an exact type or name.
If no match is found, returns a not-found hint to use `component_list`.
Use this tool before selecting or configuring any component.
For detailed info on a specific component, use `component_get_guide`.

query.description: Component type (e.g. 'XML_EXTRACT') or display name (e.g. 'XML Extract') to search for.

includeDeprecated.description: Include deprecated components in results (default: false).

job_get_log.name: job_get_log
job_get_log.description:
Fetch the execution log for a graph or jobflow run by its runId.

Returns the unstructured text of the execution log — identical to what is shown
in the CloverDX Server Execution History UI. Use to inspect diagnostic messages
for a failed run, audit a specific execution, or retrieve log output for debugging.

The response is capped at 1 MiB (1048576 bytes). For longer logs the returned
text contains the first 1 MiB followed by an explicit truncation marker — the
full log is then available via the CloverDX Server Execution History UI or on
the server's file system.

runId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the job execution (run ID).

report_support_issue.name: report_support_issue
report_support_issue.description:
Reports a problem to the CloverDX Support Portal.

This tool is invoked when the user requests to report
an issue or incident directly to CloverDX Support.
The issue report can optionally include a generated
diagnostic support package for faster troubleshooting.

Before invoking this tool, the LLM must ask the user for the email address under which the issue should be submitted.
The email is mandatory and must be explicitly confirmed by the user.
The LLM must also validate that the provided email address is in a valid email format (e.g., name@example.com).
If the user provides an invalid email address, the LLM must request the email again until a valid one is confirmed.

Parameters:
- **email** (required): Email address of the user reporting the issue. Must be obtained from the user before the tool is executed.
- **description** (required): Text description of the problem or incident.
- **subject** (required): Subject line summarizing the issue.
- **includeSupportPackage** (optional): Whether to attach a diagnostic
  package with logs and configuration details (default: true).

includeSupportPackage.description: Attach a support package (logs, configs) to the report (default: true).

emailFrom.description: Email address of the user reporting the issue.

subject.description: Subject of message which summary the issue.

description.description: Detailed description of the problem to report.

job_await.name: job_await
job_await.description:
Block until a graph or jobflow run completes or the timeout is reached.

Polls the job status server-side and returns the final status once the job reaches
a terminal state (FINISHED_OK, ERROR, ABORTED). On timeout, returns the last known
status with timedOut=true; safe to re-call with the same runId.

Use immediately after `job_run` to synchronously wait for completion.
For full execution log use `job_get_log`; for tracking details use `job_get_tracking`.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait before returning. Defaults to 300.

runId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the job execution (run ID).

stopTime.description: ISO 8601 stop timestamp, null if still running.

startTime.description: ISO 8601 start timestamp, null if not yet started.

error.description: Error details if status is ERROR, null otherwise.

status.description: Final execution status: FINISHED_OK, ERROR, ABORTED, N_A.

job_abort.name: job_abort
job_abort.description:
Abort a running graph or jobflow execution identified by runId.

Also terminates child jobs spawned by this execution.
Returns the current status if the job has already finished (no-op).

runId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the job execution to abort.
Run ID of the aborted job.

killedRunIds.description: List of run IDs that were killed (includes child jobs).

abortRequested.description: Whether the abort was successfully requested.

note_add.name: note_add
note_add.description:
Append a note under a named section to session-scoped working memory.
Creates the section if it does not exist. Use for ephemeral findings,
intermediate state, and short summaries shared between sub-agent and
outer agent within a single MCP session. Notes survive only until the
MCP session ends or `note_clear` is called — for facts that must outlive
the session, write to DECISIONS.md in the project sandbox instead.

section.description: Section name to append the note to (e.g. 'findings', '_summary', '_needs_clarification').

note_clear.name: note_clear
note_clear.description:
Clear notes from session-scoped working memory. When 'section' is set,
removes only that section; otherwise removes all sections.
See `note_add` for write semantics and the session/DECISIONS.md trade-off.

section.description: Section name to clear. Omit to clear all sections.

sandbox_list_files.name: sandbox_list_files
sandbox_list_files.description:
List files and folders in a sandbox directory. Set folderOnly=true to return directories only.

Returns:
  - files: array of file/folder entries
    - files[].isFolder: whether the entry is a folder (boolean)
    - files[].name: file or folder name (string)
    - files[].path: full path relative to the sandbox root (string)
    - files[].lastModified: last modification timestamp in milliseconds (number)
    - files[].size: file size in bytes (0 for folders) (number)

sandbox_git.name: sandbox_git
sandbox_git.description:
Unified sandbox git tool. Performs version-control operations on a sandbox's local git repository (stored under assistant/.git-assistant/ as a separate gitdir). Required: action, sandboxCode. All other parameters depend on the chosen action.

Actions:
• commit  — Stage and commit. Lazy-inits the repo on first call. Required: message. Optional: paths (defaults to git add -A).
• log     — List recent commits. Optional: limit (default 30), path, grep (message filter), since (ISO-8601 date, e.g. 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z).
• show    — Read a file at a historical commit. Required: ref, path. Do NOT use for current working-tree reads.
• diff    — Diff between two refs or a ref and the working tree. Optional: fromRef (default HEAD), toRef (default working tree), path.
• status  — Show working-tree status: staged, changed, unstaged, deleted, untracked lists.
• branch  — Manage branches. Required: op (list|create|switch|delete). Required for create/switch/delete: name.
• restore — Restore file(s) to a ref or HEAD. Required: paths. Optional: ref.
• reset   — Move HEAD or unstage files. Optional: mode (soft|mixed|hard, default mixed), ref, paths. With paths = unstage only.
• stash   — Manage stash. Required: op (push|pop|apply|drop|list). Optional: message (push), stashIndex (0-based, default 0).
• init    — Explicitly initialize the repo (otherwise auto-initialized on first commit).

message.description: Commit message (action=commit). When working inside a named project, prefix with '[<project-name>]'. Append 'Sprint: S<id>' trailer when relevant.

grep.description: Filter log commits whose message matches this string.

path.description: Sandbox-relative path to restrict log or diff output.

paths.description: Sandbox-relative paths. For commit: paths to stage (default all). For restore/reset: required path list.

limit.description: Max commits to return for log (default 30).

toRef.description: End ref for diff (default working tree).

mode.description: Reset mode (default mixed). Ignored when paths are supplied.

since.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; log returns only commits after this date (e.g. '2025-01-01T00:00:00Z').

ref.description: Commit ref (SHA, HEAD~N, branch name). Used by show, restore, reset.

knowledge_project_store.name: knowledge_project_store
knowledge_project_store.description:
Store (overwrite) a project-local knowledge entry under
<sandbox>/assistant/<projectName>/knowledge_project/[<topic>/]<name>.md.
Use to persist project-specific facts that the agent should recall in later sessions:
business rules, naming conventions, sandbox quirks, validated investigation results.
Frontmatter (name, description, tags, scope, provenance, created, updated, topic) is
added automatically. Overwriting preserves the original created date.
The server also rebuilds INDEX.md after every store — a topic-grouped overview the
agent can read via `knowledge_project_read` with a blank name.
If an entry with the same name already exists in a different topic, the old file is
deleted and the entry is relocated to the new topic (names are unique per project).
Project-bound only; do NOT use for platform-wide truth (that ships in CloverDXMCPKnowledge).

projectName.description: Project name within the sandbox (e.g. 'dwh-q4-refresh'). Entries live under <sandbox>/assistant/<projectName>/knowledge_project/.

name.description: Unique entry name (used as filename without extension). Alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores, and dots only.

topic.description: Optional grouping subdirectory (e.g. 'conventions', 'gotchas', 'decisions', 'patterns'). Lets the agent organise related entries. If omitted or blank, the entry lands at the project knowledge root.

content.description: Full Markdown body of the entry.

sandboxCode.description: Code of the project sandbox to write into.

graph_edit_properties.name: graph_edit_properties
graph_edit_properties.description:
Set or update a property on one or more existing elements via XML DOM in any
CloverDX job — graph (.grf), jobflow (.jbf), subgraph (.sgrf), and other job types.
Single-edit: provide element_type, element_id, attribute_name, value.
Bulk edit: provide a changes[] array - all changes applied atomically; fails entirely
if any change is invalid. Use dry_run=true to preview. graph_path and sandbox apply
to all changes in both modes.

Plain attribute_name (for example 'recordsNumber', 'joinType', 'fileURL') sets an
XML attribute directly. 'attr:X' sets an <attr name='X'> child with auto CDATA
wrapping. For Metadata, use attribute_name='record' with full <Record>...</Record>
XML. External metadata (.fmt files) cannot be modified here.
Always call `job_validate` after using this tool.

graph_path.description: Path to the CloverDX job file within the sandbox — graph (.grf), jobflow (.jbf), subgraph (.sgrf), etc. (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.grf').

changes.description: Bulk edit array. Mutually exclusive with single-edit params.

value.description: New value. For 'attr:': do NOT wrap in CDATA yourself.

attribute_name.description: Plain name -> XML attribute. 'attr:X' -> CDATA child. For Metadata: 'record'.

element_id.description: Element identifier. Matches 'id' attribute (or 'name' for GraphParameter).

element_type.description: Element type. GraphParameter matches by 'name'; all others match by 'id'.

sandbox_patch_file.name: sandbox_patch_file
sandbox_patch_file.description:
Patch a sandbox file using anchor-based line replacements.
Each patch locates an anchor string, applies fromOffset/toOffset to define the
replacement range, then all patches are applied bottom-up.
Anchor matching is literal against the raw file content after UTF-8 decode; no HTML/XML entity decoding or escaping is applied.
Supports dryRun=true for preview.

USE FOR: non-graph text files (.txt, .ctl, .prm, .csv, .sql, etc.).
DO NOT USE FOR graph (.grf) or jobflow (.jbf) files -- use the graph edit tools instead:
  `graph_edit_structure`  - add/delete/move whole elements (Metadata, Node, Edge, Phase, ...)
  `graph_edit_properties` - set attributes, CTL code, metadata records on existing elements
The graph_edit_* tools operate on the XML DOM and are far more reliable for graph edits.

dryRun.description: Validate and preview patches without writing the file (default: false)

patches.description: Array of patch specifications to apply.

newContent.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the target range.

toOffset.description: Line offset from anchor line to end of replacement (inclusive).

anchor.description: Unique literal substring used to locate the target line. Matching is trim-insensitive and does not perform HTML/XML entity decoding.

fromOffset.description: Line offset from anchor line to start of replacement.

anchorOccurrence.description: Optional 1-based occurrence index if anchor appears multiple times.

sandboxPath.description: Full file path within the sandbox (e.g. 'data_in/myfile.txt')

sandbox_create_directory.name: sandbox_create_directory
sandbox_create_directory.description: Create a directory in a CloverDX sandbox. Parent directory must already exist.

knowledge_project_delete.name: knowledge_project_delete
knowledge_project_delete.description:
Delete a project-local knowledge entry by name from
<sandbox>/assistant/<projectName>/knowledge_project/.
The server locates the entry across all topic subdirectories
(names are unique per project) and rebuilds INDEX.md after deletion.
Idempotent: if the entry does not exist, returns a "not found" message
rather than an error.

sandboxCode.description: Code of the project sandbox the entry lives in.

sandbox_read_file.name: sandbox_read_file
sandbox_read_file.description:
Read a plain-text file from a sandbox and return its raw content directly, with no conversion or decoding.
Use this for any text-based format that is directly readable as-is: .txt, .csv, .json, .xml, .md, source code, CloverDX graphs, etc.
Do NOT use this for binary or rich-document formats like PDF (.pdf) — use `sandbox_analyze_file` action=extract_pdf for those.
Optionally read a line range via start_line + line_count.
start_line: 1-based; negative counts from end (-1 = last line).
Optional encoding (defaults to utf-8).
Set encoding='detect' to return detected encoding instead of file content.
Max response: 1 MiB.

line_count.description: Optional number of lines to read. Must be provided together with start_line.

start_line.description: Optional starting line number. 1-based for positive values; negative values count from end (-1 is last line). Must be provided together with line_count.

encoding.description: Optional text encoding used to decode file content (default: utf-8). Use 'detect' to return only the detected encoding name instead of file content.

sandboxPath.description: Full file path within the sandbox (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.grf')

knowledge_project_search.name: knowledge_project_search
knowledge_project_search.description:
Search project-local knowledge entries stored under
<sandbox>/assistant/<projectName>/knowledge_project/ (including all topic subdirectories).
Use for recalling agent- or user-authored project facts: business rules,
naming conventions, sandbox-local quirks discovered in earlier sessions.
Scored by token overlap on name, tags, and description.
For a topic-grouped overview without keyword matching, call `knowledge_project_read`
with a blank name — that returns the auto-maintained INDEX.md.
This is separate from `knowledge_base_search`, which reads the read-only platform knowledge base.

projectName.description: Project name within the sandbox (e.g. 'dwh-q4-refresh'). Entries live under <sandbox>/assistant/<projectName>/knowledge_project/.

sandboxCode.description: Code of the project sandbox to search in.

limit.description: Maximum number of hits to return. Default 20.

server_db_get_schema.name: server_db_get_schema
server_db_get_schema.description:
Retrieves the table and column schema of the CloverDX Server's internal system
database — the server's own backing store for run history, users, sandboxes,
schedules, and other server-managed records.

NOT for user-defined ETL database connections configured in sandbox graphs.
To query sandbox connection targets, use `server_db_execute_query` (SELECT only)
or read the connection's .cfg file via `sandbox_read_file`.

## Behavior
Read-only metadata introspection via JDBC — does not execute arbitrary SQL.

## Returned information
- List of accessible tables
- Columns per table with data types, nullability, and key flags
- Optional indexes or constraints if available

## Use cases
- Inspect table structure before writing a system database query with `server_db_execute_query`
- Validate column names and types for diagnostic or admin queries

## Security
- System and credential tables are excluded
- No data content is returned — only schema metadata

sandbox_get_detail.name: sandbox_get_detail
sandbox_get_detail.description:
Returns detailed information about a single sandbox identified by its sandboxCode.

Returns:
  - sandboxCode: unique sandbox identifier
  - name: display name
  - description: sandbox description (may be empty)
  - rootPath: filesystem root path of the sandbox
  - ownerUsername: username of the sandbox owner
  - distributionType: one of partitioned, shared, local
  - suspended: whether the sandbox is currently suspended

graph_edit_structure.name: graph_edit_structure
graph_edit_structure.description:
Add, delete, or move whole structural elements in any CloverDX job — graph
(.grf), jobflow (.jbf), subgraph (.sgrf), and other job types — via XML DOM.
Companion to `graph_edit_properties` (which sets attribute values, CTL code, or
metadata records on existing elements).

USE FOR: adding new Metadata/Node/Edge/Phase/Connection/etc., deleting elements,
  moving a Node or Edge between Phases.
DO NOT USE FOR: changing attribute values, CTL code, or metadata records on
  existing elements — use `graph_edit_properties` for that.

Actions:
  add    - Insert a new element. Provide full element XML in element_xml.
  delete - Remove an element by its identity attribute (id or name).
  move   - Move a Node or Edge to a different Phase (target_phase_number).
           Only valid for Node and Edge.

dry_run=true previews changes without writing the file.
Always call `job_validate` after structural changes.

cascade.description: [delete only] Auto-remove dependent elements. Default: false.

element_xml.description: [add only] Full XML string of the element to insert. DictionaryEntry expects <Entry .../>.

graph_path.description: Path to the CloverDX job file within the sandbox — graph (.grf), jobflow (.jbf), subgraph (.sgrf), etc. (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.grf').

target_phase_number.description: [move only] Phase number to move the Node or Edge into.

element_id.description: [delete/move] Identity attribute value. Most types: 'id'; GraphParameter: 'name'; Phase: 'number'; DictionaryEntry: Entry 'name'.

validate.description: Run Stage 1 local validation after the operation. Default: true. Set false for batch edits.

action.description: add inserts a new element; delete removes one; move repositions a Node or Edge to another Phase.

phase_number.description: [add Node/Edge only] Phase number to insert into.

element_type.description: Type of graph element to operate on.

server_perf_logs_query.name: server_perf_logs_query
server_perf_logs_query.description:
Execute a SQL query (Apache Calcite dialect) against the CloverDX Server performance log file.
Returns CPU, memory, GC, and I/O metrics sampled every 3 seconds by the server monitor.
Use for time-series analysis of server health — peak CPU during a job run, memory trends, GC pause frequency.

NOT for job execution logs (use `server_logs_search`) or per-graph record counts (use `job_get_tracking`).

## Data volume — required sampling

Entries are recorded every 3 seconds → 1 200/hour, 28 800/day.
Querying without sampling or aggregation will exceed the 1 MB result limit and fail.

| Time range    | Recommended sampleRate  | Expected rows |
|---------------|-------------------------|---------------|
| 1–2 hours     | 1                       | ~1 200–2 400  |
| 6–12 hours    | 20–60                   | ~360–1 080    |
| 24 hours      | 60–120                  | ~480–1 440    |
| 3 days        | 120–240                 | ~720–2 160    |
| 1 week        | 240–600                 | ~1 008–1 764  |
| 1 month+      | aggregation (GROUP BY)  | <1 000        |

Target 1 000–1 500 rows. Formula: `(time_range_seconds / 3) / sampleRate`. Default sampleRate = 60.

If you get "Tool result is too large": increase sampleRate, reduce the time range,
use GROUP BY aggregation, or select fewer columns (avoid SELECT *).

## Time column — required transformation

The `time` column uses a comma as millisecond separator (e.g. `2025-12-03 07:00:12,275`).
Calcite cannot parse this as TIMESTAMP. Always use:

	CAST(REPLACE("time", ',', '.') AS TIMESTAMP)

Apply in WHERE, ORDER BY, and SELECT — never use the raw `"time"` column as a timestamp.

## Column reference

| Column            | Description |
|-------------------|-------------|
| time              | Sample timestamp (every 3 s; gaps indicate system/comm issues) |
| sysCPU            | Total system CPU % (all processes); if sysCPU >> cCPU+wCPU, other processes are consuming CPU |
| cCPU / wCPU       | CPU % of Core and Worker JVMs; Core typically stays below 10 % |
| cHeap / wHeap     | Heap usage (GB); approaching max → GC pressure or OOM risk |
| cGC / wGC         | GC activity % for Core/Worker; sustained high = memory pressure |
| hbAge             | Worker heartbeat age (s); >60 → overloaded or unresponsive Worker |
| jobs              | Running job count on this node |
| jobQueue          | Jobs waiting in queue |
| cThread / wThread | Live thread count; steadily rising = thread leak or blocking tasks |
| swap              | Memory swapped to disk (GB); high → severe performance degradation |
| cFD / wFD         | Open file descriptors; high/rising → "Too many open files" risk |
| cUptime / wUptime | Process uptime (s); resets to 0 on restart |

## Constraints

- SELECT only — INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE are rejected
- Column names must be double-quoted: `"sysCPU"`, `"cHeap"`, etc.
- `#logFile#` is replaced by the actual log file path automatically
- LIMIT 100 applied automatically if omitted

## Examples

```sql
-- Last 10 minutes, full detail
SELECT CAST(REPLACE("time", ',', '.') AS TIMESTAMP) AS ts, "sysCPU", "cCPU", "wCPU"
FROM #logFile#
WHERE CAST(REPLACE("time", ',', '.') AS TIMESTAMP) >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '10' MINUTE
ORDER BY ts DESC
```

```sql
-- Last 24 hours, hourly averages (safe for large time ranges)
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', CAST(REPLACE("time", ',', '.') AS TIMESTAMP)) AS hour,
       AVG("sysCPU"), MAX("cHeap")
FROM #logFile#
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour DESC
```

## Reference
- [CloverDX Performance Logs](https://doc.cloverdx.com/latest/operations/logging.html#id_performance_logs)
- [Apache Calcite](https://calcite.apache.org/)

query.description: A valid SQL query (calcite.apache.org) to execute against the performance log.

sampleRate.description: Return every Nth row (1 = all, default = 60).

component_get_guide.name: component_get_guide
component_get_guide.description:
Fetch the in-depth Markdown reference for a CloverDX component — full syntax, config
rules, mapping/CTL examples, and the gotchas the catalog (`component_get_info`) only
labels opaquely (e.g. validatorRules, xmlMapping, hashJoinKey).
Call this after `component_get_info` when the property list alone is not enough to
configure a mapping-heavy or otherwise complex component.
Lookup is by component type key (case-insensitive; e.g. 'XML_EXTRACT').

Optionally pass `filter` — a list of section keys — to return ONLY those sections
instead of the whole document (cheaper and focused). Omit it for the full document.
Valid section keys: description, purpose, xml, properties, ports, ctl, definition,
examples, mistakes, notes. Unknown keys, and sections a component does not have, are
ignored (never an error). Example: filter=["ctl","ports","mistakes"] for CTL2 authoring.
If the documentation is missing, returns the list of available keys so you can
retry with a valid type.

filter.description: Optional. Canonical section keys to return: description, purpose, xml, properties, ports, ctl, definition, examples, mistakes, notes. Omit for the whole document. Unknown or absent sections are ignored.

componentType.description: Component type key (e.g. 'XML_EXTRACT'). Case-insensitive; use the exact type string from `component_get_info` or `component_list`.

ctl_validate.name: ctl_validate
ctl_validate.description:
Validates standalone CTL2 code against explicit port metadata — no graph file needed.

componentType -> required entry point(s):
- reformat, joiner: transform()
- normalizer: count() + transform(integer)
- denormalizer: append() + transform()
- partition: getOutputPort() (input metadata only — no outputMetadata, no $out writes)
- filter: 'code' is a bare boolean expression — no function wrapper, no return,
  no $out writes (input metadata only)
- rollup: initGroup(<AccType>), updateGroup(<AccType>), finishGroup(<AccType>),
  updateTransform(integer, <AccType>), transform(integer, <AccType>) — with a group
  accumulator, pass accumulatorMetadata and use a type name matching its <Record name>;
  without one, omit accumulatorMetadata and use the built-in VoidMetadata type
- expression: 'code' is a single CTL2 expression of any type (not just boolean) —
  no function wrapper, no entry-point contract
- generic: any other CTL2 code (global scope, any functions) for any component or
  purpose — checks only that the code is compilable; no entry functions are required

For expression and generic, inputMetadata and outputMetadata are both optional —
provide them only when the code references $in.N/$out.N ports or declares variables
or function parameters typed by a metadata <Record name>.

Metadata: one .fmt <Record> XML doc per port, in port order. joiner port 0 = driver,
ports 1+ = slaves.

Known unresolvable at this scope (reported as ERROR, not silently skipped): lookup
tables, sequences, dictionary entries, Java transform classes. If your CTL only fails
because of these, that's expected — not a real bug in your code.

Error reporting: structural errors (missing ';', bad port refs) fail fast — fix and
re-run to see what's next. Once the code parses, remaining semantic errors (type
mismatches, undeclared functions, unresolved lookups/sequences) are reported together.

Returns PASS only when no ERROR-severity problems remain.

code.description: CTL2 source code (full transform), the boolean filter expression when componentType=filter, or a single CTL2 expression of any type when componentType=expression.

accumulatorMetadata.description: One .fmt XML <Record> document describing the rollup group accumulator record. Only used when componentType=rollup. The accumulator type name in your CTL must match the name attribute of this <Record>. Omit for rollups without a group accumulator — their functions use the built-in VoidMetadata type instead.

componentType.description: Component family the CTL code targets.

inputMetadata.description: One CloverDX .fmt XML document (<Record> root) per input port, in port order. Required for all component types except expression and generic, where it is optional.

outputMetadata.description: One .fmt XML document per output port, in port order. Required for reformat, joiner, rollup (at least one) and normalizer, denormalizer (exactly one); ignored for partition and filter; optional for expression and generic.

line.description: 1-based line of the problem in the CTL code (compile stage) or metadata XML (metadata stage).

stage.description: Validation stage that produced the problem: metadata (parsing .fmt XML), compile (CTL compilation), or init (entry-function and global-scope checks).

endColumn.description: 1-based end column of the problem range.

hint.description: Optional hint how to fix the problem.

portType.description: For metadata-stage problems: input, output, or accumulator.

port.description: For metadata-stage problems: zero-based port index of the invalid metadata document (always 0 for accumulator).

endLine.description: 1-based end line of the problem range.

overall.description: Validation result: PASS if no ERROR-severity problems were found, FAIL otherwise.

server_deployment.name: server_deployment
server_deployment.description:
Returns CloverDX Server deployment information. Use the `type` parameter to select:

**type=current** (default) — snapshot of the running environment:
properties (SMTP, cluster, security, database, job queue),
system info (OS, JVM, memory, GC), and runtime context (env
variables, system properties).

Architecture context: CloverDX Server uses a split-process
model — a Core JVM for management and a separate Worker JVM
for job execution. Cluster deployments consist of multiple
Core nodes, each with its own Worker, sharing a system database.

Call once per session, or whenever environment-dependent decisions
are needed (SQL dialect, available features, supported integrations).
The deployment state is stable for the lifetime of the running
server — cache the result mentally and reuse.

**type=supported** — the official support matrix for this CloverDX Server
version: validated Operating Systems, Java runtimes, Databases, and
Application Servers.

Typical workflow for compatibility check:
1. Call `server_deployment` (type=current) to get current environment.
2. Call `server_deployment` (type=supported) to get the support matrix.
3. Compare to spot unsupported OS, JVM, or database.

## Call when
- User asks about configuration, environment, JVM/memory, database type,
  or cluster topology → type=current.
- User asks what environments/versions are officially supported → type=supported.
- Checking compatibility of current deployment → call both.

## Do NOT call
- For trivial questions (CTL syntax, sandbox listings, graph editing,
  job execution, file reads/writes, status checks).
- type=current more than once per session — re-call only if the user
  explicitly says the server was restarted or reconfigured mid-session.

type.description: What to return: 'current' (default) = running environment snapshot; 'supported' = official support matrix.

meta.purpose: CloverDX Server deployment information — current environment or supported matrix

job_plan.name: job_plan
job_plan.description:
Record a structured graph design plan before writing XML.
Validates internal consistency and surfaces issues before implementation.

WHEN: After component lookups (`component_get_info` / `component_list` / `component_get_guide`), BEFORE `sandbox_write_file`.
Call `sandbox_list_assets` first to discover existing shared assets.

Validates:
- Edge source/target IDs exist in components[]
- CTL components have ctl_entry_points declared
- Sort-requiring components (DENORMALIZER, MERGE, DEDUP, EXT_MERGE_JOIN) have upstream sort
- Edge metadata_ids exist in metadata[]
- Referenced connections/lookups/sequences exist in global_assets
Returns plan with consistency warnings.

edges.description: All edges. Use exact port strings from `component_get_info`.

metadata.description: Exactly one of: (1) ID of a metadata record declared in metadata[] (e.g. 'MetaOrder') — must exist there; (2) reference to another edge that already has metadata assigned: '#//Edge0'; (3) empty string for auto-propagation from the connected component.

id.description: Edge ID — unique within the graph (e.g. 'Edge0').

purpose.description: Brief: source, transformation, and target. Used as graph description.

graph_path.description: Intended file path within the sandbox (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.grf').

reference_graphs.description: Paths to existing graphs consulted as patterns before designing.

components.description: All component nodes. Call `component_get_info` for each type before filling.

ctl_entry_points.description: Required CTL functions (e.g. ['transform()']). Must declare for any CTL component.

key_config.description: The most important configuration note for this component.

debug_input.description: Set true for test-data source nodes in subgraphs (debugInput='true').

purpose.description: What this component does in this specific graph.

debug_output.description: Set true for test-data sink nodes in subgraphs (debugOutput='true').

phase.description: Phase number this component belongs to (default 0).

id.description: Node ID — unique within the graph, ALLCAPS_N convention (e.g. 'ORDER_VALIDATOR').

graph_name.description: Name of the graph being designed (becomes the 'name' attribute on <Graph>).

phases.description: Execution phases. Most graphs use single phase 0. Add phases only for sequential dependencies.

purpose.description: Why this phase is separate from the previous one.

metadata.description: All metadata definitions. Every edge must reference one.

risks.description: Known risks to verify before writing (e.g. sort requirements, CDATA nesting, existing assets to reuse).

public.description: Whether exposed as a public parameter.

required.description: Whether a value must be supplied at runtime.

subgraphs.description: SUBGRAPH components. Verify port counts and required parameters before filling.

output_ports.description: Number of output ports this subgraph exposes.

input_ports.description: Number of input ports this subgraph exposes.

component_id.description: Node ID of the SUBGRAPH component (e.g. 'EXTRACT').

ctl_imports.description: External .ctl files via import or transformURL.

used_by.description: Component IDs whose CTL imports this file.

provides.description: Brief note on what functions this file provides.

lookup_tables.description: Lookup tables for LOOKUP_JOIN or CTL lookup('id').get(...).

used_by.description: Component IDs or CTL locations referencing this lookup.

id.description: Lookup table ID as referenced in CTL and LOOKUP_JOIN.

connections.description: Database/service connections referenced by component dbConnection attributes.

cfg_path.description: Plan field only — path to the .cfg file when source='external', e.g. '${CONN_DIR}/MyDB.cfg'. In generated XML: dbConfig= for type=JDBC, config= for all other types. Never use cfg_path as an XML attribute.

source.description: 'external'=backed by a .cfg file (preferred); 'inline'=all attributes embedded in graph XML.

type.description: Connection type. Determines the XML type= attribute on <Connection>.

used_by.description: Component IDs that reference this connection.

id.description: Connection ID — unique within the graph, referenced by dbConnection= on components (e.g. 'DWHConn').

sequences.description: Sequences for CTL sequence('id').next(). Missing declaration fails at runtime.

id.description: Sequence ID as referenced in CTL (e.g. 'RecordSeq').

used_by.description: Component IDs whose CTL calls this sequence.

global_assets.description: <Global> section assets beyond metadata. Missing declarations cause validation/runtime failures. Call `sandbox_list_assets` first.

graph_resolve_edge_schemas.name: graph_resolve_edge_schemas
graph_resolve_edge_schemas.description:
Resolve what record schema (field names, types, nullability) would flow along
each edge of a CloverDX graph/jobflow at runtime, using the engine's metadata propagation.

Use this when inspecting a static graph where edges have no explicit metadata
assigned in the XML — the engine often derives the schema automatically (e.g.
a SORT propagates its input schema unchanged to the output).

Useful for:
- Understanding what data flows between components before editing a graph
- Verifying that a transformation outputs the expected fields
- Debugging schema mismatches without running the graph

For each edge, returns:
- metadataSource: how the schema was determined
  - EXPLICIT: defined directly on this edge in the graph XML
  - REFERENCED: this edge points to another edge's metadata (see metadataRefEdge);
    fields are fully resolved through the reference
  - PROPAGATED: not defined on the edge; engine derived it from a neighbouring edge
  - NONE: no schema and none is expected (e.g. jobflow control edges)
- metadataName: name of the resolved record schema, or null for NONE
- fields: full field list (name, type, nullable) — populated for EXPLICIT,
  REFERENCED, and PROPAGATED; empty for NONE

By default all edges are returned. Pass edgeIds to restrict to specific edges.

jobFile.description: Path to the graph(.grf) or jobflow(.jbf) file within the sandbox (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.grf').

edgeIds.description: Optional list of edge IDs to include in the result. When omitted, all edges are returned. Must not be empty. Unknown IDs cause an error.

sandboxCode.description: Code of the sandbox containing the job file.

edges.description: Map of edge ID to its resolved metadata. Contains every edge in the root graph, or only the requested edges if edge_ids was supplied.

metadataName.description: Name of the resolved metadata record, or null when metadataSource is NONE.

hasMetadata.description: True if a schema could be resolved for this edge (metadataSource is EXPLICIT, REFERENCED, or PROPAGATED).

metadataSource.description: How the schema was determined. EXPLICIT: defined directly on this edge in the XML. REFERENCED: this edge links to another edge's metadata (see metadataRefEdge); fields are resolved through the reference. PROPAGATED: not defined on the edge, but the engine derived it from a neighbouring edge during propagation. NONE: the edge legitimately has no schema and none is expected.

metadataRefEdge.description: When metadataSource is REFERENCED, the ID of the edge whose metadata this edge points to (the metadataRef target); otherwise null.

fields.description: Fields of the resolved schema, fully populated for EXPLICIT, REFERENCED, and PROPAGATED. Empty when metadataSource is NONE.

type.description: CloverDX field type name (e.g. string, integer, date).

nullable.description: Whether the field accepts null values.

sandbox_copy_file.name: sandbox_copy_file
sandbox_copy_file.description:
Copy a file within or across sandboxes. Overwrites destination if it exists.
Always back up a graph (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.bak.grf') before large edits.

sourceSandboxPath.description: Full source file path within the source sandbox (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.grf')

sourceSandboxCode.description: Sandbox code containing the source file

destSandboxCode.description: Sandbox code for the destination. Omit or set to the same value as sourceSandboxCode for an intra-sandbox copy.

destSandboxPath.description: Full destination file path (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.bak.grf'). Directory must already exist.

job_list.name: job_list
job_list.description:
List recent graph and jobflow executions from the CloverDX Server execution history.

Filter by sandbox, jobFile (substring), or status. Returns runId, status, timestamps,
duration, and error info. Results are ordered by start time descending (newest first).
Use to find runIds for other job_* tools.

Status values: RUNNING, FINISHED_OK, ERROR, ABORTED, N_A.
Note: the status filter parameter accepts only the four explicit
values; N_A appears in results but cannot be used as a filter value.
Use limit and offset for pagination.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default 20, max 100.

jobFile.description: Filter by job file path (partial match).

sandboxCode.description: Filter by an existing sandbox code.

status.description: Filter by execution status. One of: RUNNING, FINISHED_OK, ERROR, ABORTED.

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Default 0.

returned.description: Number of executions returned in this response.

job_run.name: job_run
job_run.description:
Submit a graph or jobflow for async execution. Returns the assigned runId immediately.

Follow-up tools: `job_await` (block until completion), `job_get_status` (poll status),
`job_get_log` (retrieve log), `job_get_tracking` (record counts per component),
`job_get_edge_debug_data` (per-edge sampled records — requires debug=true).
Use the params object to pass job parameter overrides as key-value pairs.
Set debug=true for edge debug data capture.

jobFile.description: Path to the job file within the sandbox (e.g. graph/MyGraph.grf).

params.description: Optional key-value pairs passed as job parameters.

sandboxCode.description: Code of the sandbox containing the job.

debug.description: Enable edge debug data capture (default: false). Required for `job_get_edge_debug_data` to return data.

runId.description: Run ID assigned to the new execution.

knowledge_base_search.name: knowledge_base_search
knowledge_base_search.description:
Search the read-only CloverDX MCP Knowledge base (guides, recipes, troubleshooting
— shipped in the CloverDXMCPKnowledge library; per-component reference now lives in
`component_get_guide`). Content is fetched fresh from the library on every call
(no caching).
Returns a JSON array of matching entries; each item has name, description, tags,
source, and category (lane). Default matchMode='literal' scores by token overlap on
name (word-boundary +3, substring +2), tags (+2 per match), and description (+1).
Tokens are case-insensitive and dropped if shorter than 2 chars. Set matchMode='regex'
to treat the whole query as a single regex applied to name/description/tags (case-
insensitive). Use the category param to restrict to a single lane.
For project-scoped agent-curated notes use `knowledge_project_search` instead.

matchMode.description: Match mode: 'literal' (default, token-based) or 'regex' (case-insensitive regex against name/description/tags).

query.description: Search query. With matchMode='literal' (default) tokenised on non-alphanumeric. With matchMode='regex' the whole string is a regex.

category.description: Optional lane filter: guides, recipes, or troubleshooting. Omit to search all lanes.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default: 20.

job_validate.name: job_validate
job_validate.description:
Validates a graph or jobflow file using server-side checkConfig.

Runs deep configuration validation: checks component settings, connections,
metadata compatibility, and attribute values. Returns a list of problems
with severity (ERROR, WARNING, INFO) and location details.

Overall result is PASS only when no ERROR-severity problems are found.
Warnings and info messages are reported but do not cause FAIL.

For parameterized jobs, job_validate may report errors or warnings
that do not occur at runtime, because validation does not receive
runtime parameter values. Interpret such findings with caution.

Errors may not be exhaustive — some block further checks. Fix reported
issues and re-validate until the result is PASS.

jobFile.description: Path to the graph or jobflow file within the sandbox (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.grf').

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for validation to complete. Defaults to 120.

sandboxCode.description: Sandbox code containing the job file.

overall.description: Validation result: PASS if no errors found, FAIL otherwise.

severity.description: Problem severity: ERROR, WARNING, or INFO.

exceptionStackTrace.description: Truncated stack trace of the underlying exception, when present.

exceptionMessage.description: Underlying exception message chain, when the problem carries a cause.

attributeName.description: Attribute name related to the problem.

elementName.description: Name of the graph element with the problem.

elementId.description: ID of the graph element with the problem.

timedOut.description: True if the operation timed out before completing.

think.name: think
think.description:
Log explicit reasoning before acting. Returns acknowledgement only.

MUST use before:
- Choosing between components (reason through criteria)
- Writing or editing a graph (plan components, edges, metadata)
- Fixing validation errors (diagnose root cause first)
- Following a reference graph pattern

thought.description: Your reasoning, plan, hypothesis, or decision rationale.

sandbox_grep_files.name: sandbox_grep_files
sandbox_grep_files.description:
Search file contents across one or more sandboxes (like grep -rn).
Supports literal or regex matching, optional file glob filtering,
optional path scoping, and optional context lines around matches.

Examples:
- Find graphs using a component: searchString='type="VALIDATOR"', sandboxes=['DWH'], sandboxPath='graph'
- Regex search in CTL files: searchString='function\s+[A-Za-z_]+', matchMode='regex', filePattern='*.ctl'

Files larger than 10 MB are skipped; they appear in the `skipped` array with reason `file_too_large`.

filePattern.description: Optional shell-style wildcard to filter files before content search. Defaults to '*' (all files).

sandboxPath.description: Optional directory prefix within each sandbox to search recursively under. Defaults to sandbox root.

maxResultsPerSandbox.description: Maximum number of matches to return per sandbox. Default: 25, max: 200.

contextLines.description: Number of lines to include before and after each matched line. Default: 0.

searchString.description: Exact string or regex pattern to search for. Must not be blank (must contain at least one non-whitespace character).

matchMode.description: Match mode: literal string match or regex. Default: literal.

server_logs_search.name: server_logs_search
server_logs_search.description:
Lists server log entries filtered by a regular expression pattern and appender type, within a specified time interval.

Returns up to 1MB of log data per call.

To retrieve all matching entries, use pagination:
	- Call repeatedly, passing the timestamp of the last message from the previous response (found in the 'logs' field) as the fromTimestamp parameter in the next request.
	- **Stop pagination when:**
		- The 'moreData' field in the response is false (indicating you've reached the end)
		- You've reached the toTimestamp limit
	- **Only continue pagination if 'moreData' is true**, as this indicates there may be more matching entries available.

	This way, each subsequent call continues fetching logs after the last returned timestamp until no more results are available.

	Parameters:
		- pattern: Java regex to filter log entries.
		- appender: Which log appender to query.
		- fromTimestamp: Start of the time interval (inclusive). For pagination, set this to the timestamp of the last message from the previous response. Format: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss,SSS.
		- toTimestamp: End of the time interval (exclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss,SSS.

	Response:
		- logs: String containing the log entries.
		- moreData: Boolean indicating if there are more entries to retrieve (true = more data available, false = no more data).

pattern.description: Regular expression pattern in Java format (java.util.regex.Pattern) to filter log entries

appender.description:
Specifies which	log appender to retrieve logs from.
	Available options are:

		- ALL: It contains information related to Server core and worker processes, start and end times of job executions, successful and unsuccessful logins, etc.
- NODE_STATUS: It contains cluster-related messages. It contains information on job delegation across nodes and other types of messages related to cluster communication.
- USER_ACTION: It contains user-related operations, e.g. login, logout, user creation, and file synchronization triggered by changes in Server projects.
- SERVER_AUDIT_LOG: It contains information about operations triggered by the CloverDX Server core, e.g., job execution calls. This log is disabled by default. Refer here for more information about how to enable it and what kind of information it logs.
- SERVER_INTEGRATION: It contains information related to the interaction between CloverDX Designer and Server.
- DATA_SERVICE: It contains information related to data services, e.g., login information, target URI, IP address, or returned HTTP code.
- JOB_QUEUE: It contains information related to jobs processing, e.g., the number of currently queued and running jobs, and the current system CPU.
- MONITOR: It contains information related to monitors, e.g., creation and deletion of monitors, changes in monitor states, or the number of failing items in monitors.
- REMOTE_DATA_MANAGER: It contains details of remote access to data sets in the Data Manager if remote Data Manager is configured. It includes information like the IP address of the remote Server, the configured user and client name of the remote connection, the type of action performed (such as read or write), and how long the operation took.
- ASSISTANT_WRANGLER: It contains information related to the AI Assistant Wrangler feature, e.g., requests made to the assistant and responses received.
- WORKER: It contains worker-related information (e.g. when a worker process was stopped or started, and it lists job start and end times

fromTimestamp.description: The start of the time interval (inclusive). For pagination, set this to the timestamp of the last log message from the previous response to continue retrieving subsequent entries.

toTimestamp.description: The end of the time interval (exclusive). Only log entries with timestamps earlier than this value are returned.

note_read.name: note_read
note_read.description:
Read notes from session-scoped working memory. When 'section' is set,
returns only that section's contents (empty string if not present);
otherwise returns all sections inlined in full while the board is small, or a lightweight index of section names with sizes once it grows past the inline limit (call note_read with a section name to read that section's contents).
See `note_add` for write semantics and the session/DECISIONS.md trade-off.

section.description: Section name to read. Omit to read all sections.

sandbox_write_file.name: sandbox_write_file
sandbox_write_file.description:
Write a file in a sandbox using one of four modes: overwrite (default), append, insert, replace.
insert requires start_line and shifts existing lines down.
replace requires start_line + line_count and replaces that line range with the provided content.

start_line.description: 1-based line position. Required for insert and replace.

content.description: UTF-8 text to write. For insert/replace, content is inserted by lines.

line_count.description: Number of lines to replace. Required for replace only.

sandbox_list_assets.name: sandbox_list_assets
sandbox_list_assets.description:
List reusable assets in a sandbox. Asset types are recognized by file extension:
metadata (.fmt), connections (.cfg), lookups (.lkp), CTL (.ctl), sequences (.seq),
parameters (.prm).
Call early during graph creation to discover shared assets and their fileURL
paths before defining anything inline. Filter by assetType to narrow results.

Use detail=verbose to parse file contents and return enriched metadata
alongside the paths. detail=basic (default) returns paths only and is faster.

Returns:
  - sandbox: sandbox code (string)
  - asset_type: the requested asset type filter (string)
  - count: total number of distinct asset paths found (integer)
  - assets: when assetType=all, an object keyed by type; when a specific type
            is requested, a list for that type only.

Asset list entries:
  - metadata: {path, fields: [...up to 25 field names...], truncated?}
  - connection: {path, type, dbURL?, database?, jndiName?}
  - lookup: {path, type} (e.g. dbLookup, simpleLookup, persistentLookup)
  - parameters: {path, parameters: [...parameter names...]}
  - ctl: {path, functions: ["returnType name(params)", ...]}
  - sequence: plain string paths
  - any file whose content cannot be parsed: {path, content: "unknown"}

detail.description: basic (default): paths only. verbose: parse file contents — metadata fields, connection dbURL/type, lookup type, CTL functions, parameter names.

assetType.description: Filter: metadata(.fmt), connection(.cfg), lookup(.lkp), ctl(.ctl), sequence(.seq), parameters(.prm), or all (default).

job_get_tracking.name: job_get_tracking
job_get_tracking.description:
# Execution Tracking — Per-Run Phases / Nodes / Ports

Returns a structured tracking snapshot for a single graph execution: phase
timings, per-component results and CPU times, and per-port record / byte
counters. Use this to verify data flow ("filter passed N of M records") or
to debug a failed run.

## Parameters
* `runId` (required) — the numeric run identifier.
* `detailed` (optional, default `true`) — when `false`, the response is
  trimmed to just the top-level status + `summary` aggregates (phase / node
  / port counts and total records / bytes), omitting the full hierarchy.
  Useful on large graphs where the detailed payload is heavy.

## Response shape (detailed=true)
```
{
  "run_id": "12345",
  "status": "FINISHED_OK",
  "exec_seconds": 180.0,
  "phases": [{
    "phase_number": 0,
    "exec_seconds": 90.5,
    "nodes": [{
      "node_id": "READ_CSV", "node_name": "Read CSV",
      "node_type": "DATA_READER", "result": "FINISHED_OK",
      "cpu_seconds": 1.2,
      "ports": [{"port_type": "OUTPUT", "index": 0,
                 "records": 100, "bytes": 5000}]
    }]
  }],
  "summary": {"phase_count": 1, "node_count": 1, "port_count": 1,
              "total_records": 100, "total_bytes": 5000}
}
```
When tracking is not yet available (job hasn't started, or tracking wasn't
recorded), the response carries `status: "UNKNOWN"`, empty aggregates, and
a `warning` field describing the situation. The tool does not error in that
case — callers can re-poll.

## Obtaining runId
If the runId is not known in advance, use `job_list` or query the
`run_record` table via `server_db_execute_query`.

detailed.description: If false, return only the summary aggregates without the per-phase/node/port hierarchy. Default true.

runId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the job execution (run ID).

warning.description: Present only when tracking data is unavailable.

job_get_status.name: job_get_status
job_get_status.description:
Quick status check for a graph or jobflow run (no log fetch). Identifies the run by runId.

Status values: RUNNING, FINISHED_OK, ERROR, ABORTED, N_A.
RUNNING includes elapsed time and current phase number.
For completed runs, use `job_get_tracking` or `job_get_log`.

runId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the job execution (run ID).

stopTime.description: ISO 8601 stop timestamp, null if still running.

startTime.description: ISO 8601 start timestamp, null if not yet started.

error.description: Error details if status is ERROR, null otherwise.

status.description: Execution status: RUNNING, FINISHED_OK, ERROR, ABORTED, N_A.

knowledge_project_read.name: knowledge_project_read
knowledge_project_read.description:
Read a single project-local knowledge entry from
<sandbox>/assistant/<projectName>/knowledge_project/[<topic>/]<name>.md.
Returns the entry body without the YAML frontmatter; names are unique per project,
so the server auto-resolves across topic subdirectories.
If called without a name (or with a blank name), returns the auto-generated
INDEX.md — a topic-grouped overview of the project's persisted knowledge.
Use this as a cheap discovery call to see what already exists.

projectName.description: Project name within the sandbox (e.g. 'dwh-q4-refresh'). Entries live under <sandbox>/assistant/<projectName>/knowledge_project/.

name.description: Entry name (without .md extension). Omit or leave blank to list available entries in the project.

sandboxCode.description: Code of the project sandbox the entry lives in.

job_get_edge_debug_data.name: job_get_edge_debug_data
job_get_edge_debug_data.description:
Fetch sample records that flowed through an edge during a debug run.

Use to inspect mid-graph data for diagnosing transformation logic — e.g. checking
what values reached a component's reject port or an intermediate edge.
Requires the job to have been executed with edge debugging enabled
(debug=true top-level parameter on `job_run`; the legacy
edgeDebugging=true in `job_run` params still works for back-compat
but new code should use the top-level parameter). If debugging
was not enabled, the response will contain debugNotAvailable=true
with an explanation.

Records are returned as an array of field-name to string-value maps.
All field values are serialized as strings; null fields are represented as JSON null.
Use fromRecord and recordCount for pagination.

Each response also includes a metadata array — one entry per record
field with name, type, nullable, and optional format. Use this to
correctly interpret record values (e.g. parse the string with the
format pattern for date fields, or apply type-specific validation).

edgeId.description: Edge ID as defined in the graph XML (e.g. 'Edge0').

recordCount.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to 50.

runId.description: Run ID of the job execution (from `job_run` or `job_list`).

fromRecord.description: Zero-based index of the first record to return. Defaults to 0.
Zero-based index of the first returned record.

records.description: List of data records that flowed through the edge.

items.description: A single data record — field name to string value map.

debugNotAvailable.description: True when edge debugging was not enabled for this run.

edgeId.description: Edge ID for which the data was fetched.

runId.description: Run ID used to fetch the data.

metadata.description: Field metadata — name, type, nullable, and optional format for each field.

type.description: Field data type (e.g. integer, string, date, decimal).

nullable.description: Whether the field accepts null values.

format.description: Optional format pattern (e.g. date format string).

sandbox_list.name: sandbox_list
sandbox_list.description:
List all sandboxes accessible to the current user.

Each entry returns:
- sandboxCode: unique sandbox identifier — pass as 'sandboxCode' in other tool calls.
- name: display name shown in the CloverDX Server UI.
- description: free-form text from the sandbox properties (may be null when unset).
- suspended: true if the sandbox is currently suspended — pre-filter on this if
  you don't want to interact with disabled sandboxes.

server_db_execute_query.name: server_db_execute_query
server_db_execute_query.description:
Executes a read-only SQL SELECT against the CloverDX internal system database. It is for metadata,
	run history, users, schedules, and other server-managed records.

	This is NOT a query tool for user-defined data sources
	(database connections configured in sandboxes for ETL graphs).

	Typical tables: run_record, sandbox, user, library_repository,
	schedule, task, event_listener, sequence_value.

	## Database dialect
	If you don't already know the dialect from this session, call
	`server_deployment` once to identify it and reuse the result.

	If table or column structure is unclear, call
	`server_db_get_schema`.

	## Allowed

	- SELECT only — INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/etc. are rejected
	- Joins, WHERE, LIMIT, aggregations
	- Single statement (no semicolon-separated batches)

	## Forbidden

	Queries touching system/credential tables or password columns are
	rejected by the server with an explicit error message.

sqlQuery.description: SQL SELECT statement to execute against the system database.

meta.purpose: Execute validated read-only SQL SELECT queries against the CloverDX Server's database

db_execute_query.name: db_execute_query
db_execute_query.description:
Execute a SQL query against any database reachable by the CloverDX Server via JDBC.
Returns the result set as JSON (default) or delimited text (CSV).
Use 'format' to choose output format:
  "json" (default) - array of row objects; column names from the SQL AS-alias or base column name.
  "csv"            - delimited text with a header row; delimiter defaults to "|".
Use 'delimiter' to override the field separator for CSV (single character, default "|").
Use 'max_rows' to limit rows returned (1-1000, default 100);
results are truncated at 1000 regardless of the requested value.
For DML/DDL queries that produce no result set, 'rows_affected' is returned instead of rows.

## connectionProperties
Option A (preferred) - config file: pass only 'dbConfig' as a sandbox URL:
  sandbox://<sandbox_code>/<path-to-cfg> (e.g. "sandbox://mybox/conn/myDB.cfg").
  Use when a saved .cfg exists. The .cfg must not use jndiName.
Option B (fallback) - inline properties:
  jdbcSpecific: JDBC driver type identifier (see list below) — NOT the database name.
  dbURL: connection URL — database name is encoded here.
  user, password: credentials (optional).
  name: display label only — omit it.
  database: database type — typically matches jdbcSpecific (see exceptions below).
  Do not pass jndiName — JNDI is not supported.

## jdbcSpecific values and dbURL formats
  POSTGRE     jdbc:postgresql://hostname/database
  ORACLE      jdbc:oracle:thin:@host:1521:SID  |  jdbc:oracle:thin:@host:1521/service_name
  MSSQL       jdbc:sqlserver://hostname:1433;databaseName=database  (Microsoft driver, recommended)
              jdbc:jtds:sqlserver://hostname:1433/database  (legacy jTDS driver)
  MYSQL       jdbc:mysql://hostname:3306/database
  DB2         jdbc:db2://hostname:50000/database
  SQLITE      jdbc:sqlite:/path/to/file.db
  SNOWFLAKE   jdbc:snowflake://account.snowflakecomputing.com/?[params]
  REDSHIFT    jdbc:redshift://cluster.redshift.amazonaws.com:5439/database
  VERTICA     jdbc:vertica://hostname:5433/database
  DERBY       jdbc:derby://hostname:1527/derby.db
  EXASOLUTION jdbc:exa:hostname:8563;schema=schemaName
  SYBASE      jdbc:jtds:sybase://hostname:7100/database

## .cfg file generation
Set both database=<TYPE> and jdbcSpecific=<TYPE> to the same value — with one exception:
MSSQL with Microsoft JDBC driver uses database=MSSQLSERVER (not MSSQL), jdbcSpecific=MSSQL.
MSSQL with legacy jTDS driver uses database=MSSQL, jdbcSpecific=MSSQL.

format.description: Output format: "json" (default) - object with columns and rows arrays; "csv" - delimited text with a header row.

delimiter.description: Single-character field delimiter for CSV output. Default "|". Ignored for JSON format.

maxRows.description: Maximum rows to return (1-1000). Default 100. Hard cap is always 1000.

sql.description: SQL statement to execute (SELECT, DML, or DDL).

connectionProperties.description: DB connection config. Option A (preferred): {"dbConfig": "sandbox://code/path.cfg"} (must not use jndiName - JNDI is not supported). Option B (inline): {"jdbcSpecific": "POSTGRE", "dbURL": "jdbc:postgresql://hostname/dbname", "user": "u", "password": "p"}. jdbcSpecific is the JDBC driver type — NOT the database name (which belongs in dbURL). Supported: POSTGRE, ORACLE, MSSQL, MSSQL2005, MYSQL, DB2, SQLITE, SNOWFLAKE, REDSHIFT, SYBASE, VERTICA, HIVE, INFORMIX, DERBY, EXASOLUTION, FIREBIRD, PERVASIVE, MSACCESSJAVA, GENERIC. When creating a .cfg: set jdbcSpecific=<TYPE> and database=<TYPE> to the same value — EXCEPT MSSQL with Microsoft driver where database=MSSQLSERVER (not MSSQL).

sandbox_find_file.name: sandbox_find_file
sandbox_find_file.description:
Recursively find files in a sandbox by shell-style wildcard (* and ?). Client-side filtering.

Returns:
  - files: array of matched file entries
    - files[].name: file name (string)
    - files[].path: full path relative to the sandbox root (string)
    - files[].size: file size in bytes (number)
    - files[].lastModified: last modification timestamp in milliseconds (number)

sandboxPath.description: Optional starting directory within the sandbox (default: root)

sandbox_get_workspace_parameters.name: sandbox_get_workspace_parameters
sandbox_get_workspace_parameters.description:
Resolve sandbox workspace parameter values — the ${DATAIN_DIR}, ${DATAOUT_DIR},
${CONN_DIR}, and other path placeholders defined in workspace.prm — with optional
server-side overlay from server defaults and system properties.

Call this before writing any file path into a graph to get the correct resolved
values for parameters like ${DATAIN_DIR} rather than hardcoding absolute paths.

NOT for graph-level parameters defined inside a .grf file (those are graph
execution parameters passed via `job_run`'s params argument).
NOT for jobflow token parameters.

Returns resolved values with source provenance for each parameter, any overrides
applied by the server, and any still-unresolved ${...} placeholder references.

Returns:
  - sandbox: sandbox code (string)
  - workspace_param_path: path to the parameter file that was read (string)
  - resolution_scope: always "best_effort" (string)
  - counts: summary counts for each data source and resolution result (object)
  - resolved_parameters: fully resolved parameter values keyed by name (object)
  - parameter_sources: provenance of each parameter (workspace_prm, server_defaults, system_properties) (object)
  - workspace_descriptions: description text for each parameter from workspace.prm (object)
  - applied_overrides: parameters whose value were overridden by server defaults or system properties (object)
  - unresolved_references: remaining ${...} placeholder names per parameter (object)

workspaceParamPath.description: Path to workspace parameter file within sandbox (default: 'workspace.prm').

includeDefaults.description: Overlay values from the server's GetDefaults operation, which provides server-level default parameter values (default: true).

includeAllServerProperties.description: Also include server properties that have no corresponding entry in workspace.prm. Useful for discovering all available server-side parameter values (default: false).

includeSystemProperties.description: Overlay matching keys from server system properties — JVM -D flags or OS environment variables registered as system properties (default: true).

graph_list_elements.name: graph_list_elements
graph_list_elements.description:
Returns elements of a specific type from a job file (graph/subgraph/jobflow/data_service).

Retrieves lookup tables, dictionaries, sequences, or metadata
definitions from the specified graph/jobflow file. The sandbox
must be accessible to the current user.

Use the optional `id` parameter to fetch a single named element.
A non-matching id returns an empty elements list rather than an error.

Element structure varies by type:
- lookupTable / dictionary / sequence: name + properties array
- metadata: id + properties map + fields array

jobFile.description: Path to the graph/subgraph/jobflow file within the sandbox (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.grf').

sandboxCode.description: Sandbox code containing the job file.

id.description: Optional element name (for lookupTable/dictionary/sequence) or id (for metadata). If provided, only the element with an exact match is returned.

elements.description: List of matching elements. Each item shape depends on elementType: OutlineElement (name, properties, error) for lookupTable/dictionary/sequence; Metadata (id, properties, fields) for metadata.

error.description: Error message if the element could not be loaded.

oneOf.description: Represents a lookupTable, dictionary, or sequence element.

elementType.description: The requested element type: lookupTable, dictionary, sequence, or metadata.

knowledge_read_resource.name: knowledge_read_resource
knowledge_read_resource.description:
Fetch the content of a CloverDX knowledge resource by its URI. Resources are
static reference documents (text/markdown) or structured data (application/json)
from the CloverDX knowledge library installed on the server.

Call `knowledge_list_resources` first to discover available URIs.
URI format example: cloverdx://reference/graph-xml

uri.description: Full resource URI as returned by `knowledge_list_resources` (e.g. 'cloverdx://reference/graph-xml').

task_workflow_get.name: task_workflow_get
task_workflow_get.description:
MUST call at the start of any CloverDX task. Returns step-by-step agent instructions
with mandatory phases, XML rules, validation requirements, error fix procedures, and
a completion checklist for the requested task type.

This is NOT documentation about CloverDX graphs or jobflows — it returns procedural
instructions that guide the agent's own actions for the current task.

Task types:
- 'create_graph': Design and build a new ETL graph (.grf) — component selection,
  metadata definitions, XML structure rules, and validation.
- 'edit_graph': Modify an existing graph — read-first protocol, patch vs. rewrite
  decision, re-read-between-patches rule.
- 'create_edit_jobflow': Create or edit a jobflow (.jbf) — token-flow model,
  child job wiring, branch and routing rules.
- 'validate_and_run': Validate, execute, and verify a graph — Stage 1/Stage 2
  error handling, tracking inspection, log analysis.

Defaults to 'create_graph' if omitted.

sandbox_rename_file.name: sandbox_rename_file
sandbox_rename_file.description:
Rename a file in a sandbox (same directory only).
To move to a different directory, use `sandbox_copy_file` + `sandbox_delete_file`.

Returns:
  - message: status message confirming the rename operation (string)

newName.description: New filename only — no directory component (e.g. 'MyGraphV2.grf')

sandboxPath.description: Full current file path within the sandbox (e.g. 'graph/MyGraph.grf')

sandboxCode.description: Sandbox code containing the file (e.g. MySandbox)

sandbox_delete_file.name: sandbox_delete_file
sandbox_delete_file.description: Delete a file from a CloverDX sandbox. Use with caution — this is irreversible.

db_get_schema.name: db_get_schema
db_get_schema.description:
Query the schema of any database reachable by the CloverDX Server via JDBC -
not tied to a specific DB engine; works for any JDBC-compatible database
the server can connect to.
Use 'type' to select what to retrieve:
  "schemas"  - list all schemas available on the connection (no extra params needed)
  "tables"   - list tables; optionally filter by 'schema'
  "columns"  - list columns for a specific 'table'; optionally qualify with 'schema' and 'owner' (no row limit - all columns are always returned).
Always includes 'primaryKey' (list of PK column names).
Use 'detail'="full" to also include 'foreignKeys': each entry has 'column' (local FK column) and
'foreignSchema'/'foreignTable'/'foreignColumn' (the referenced PK table/column).
Note: 'primaryKey' and 'foreignKeys' require CloverDX Server 7.5 or later on the target;
older versions return columns only.
Results for "schemas" and "tables" are capped at 'maxItems' (default 250);
if the result was capped, the response includes "truncated": true.

## connectionProperties
Option A (preferred) - config file: pass only 'dbConfig' as a sandbox URL:
  sandbox://<sandbox_code>/<path-to-cfg> (e.g. "sandbox://mybox/conn/myDB.cfg").
  Use when a saved .cfg exists. The .cfg must not use jndiName.
Option B (fallback) - inline properties:
  jdbcSpecific: JDBC driver type identifier (see list below) — NOT the database name.
  dbURL: connection URL — database name is encoded here.
  user, password: credentials (optional).
  name: display label only — omit it.
  database: database type — typically matches jdbcSpecific (see exceptions below).
  Do not pass jndiName — JNDI is not supported.

## jdbcSpecific values and dbURL formats
  POSTGRE     jdbc:postgresql://hostname/database
  ORACLE      jdbc:oracle:thin:@host:1521:SID  |  jdbc:oracle:thin:@host:1521/service_name
  MSSQL       jdbc:sqlserver://hostname:1433;databaseName=database  (Microsoft driver, recommended)
              jdbc:jtds:sqlserver://hostname:1433/database  (legacy jTDS driver)
  MYSQL       jdbc:mysql://hostname:3306/database
  DB2         jdbc:db2://hostname:50000/database
  SQLITE      jdbc:sqlite:/path/to/file.db
  SNOWFLAKE   jdbc:snowflake://account.snowflakecomputing.com/?[params]
  REDSHIFT    jdbc:redshift://cluster.redshift.amazonaws.com:5439/database
  VERTICA     jdbc:vertica://hostname:5433/database
  DERBY       jdbc:derby://hostname:1527/derby.db
  EXASOLUTION jdbc:exa:hostname:8563;schema=schemaName
  SYBASE      jdbc:jtds:sybase://hostname:7100/database

## .cfg file generation
Set both database=<TYPE> and jdbcSpecific=<TYPE> to the same value — with one exception:
MSSQL with Microsoft JDBC driver uses database=MSSQLSERVER (not MSSQL), jdbcSpecific=MSSQL.
MSSQL with legacy jTDS driver uses database=MSSQL, jdbcSpecific=MSSQL.

schema.description: Schema name: filter for tables, qualifier for columns. Optional.

maxItems.description: Maximum number of items to return for type="schemas" or type="tables". No limit for columns. Default 250. If truncated, the response includes "truncated": true.

detail.description: Level of detail for type="columns": "basic" (default) returns columns and primary key; "full" also includes foreign keys. (primary key and foreign keys info not available prior to CloverDX Server 7.5).

connectionProperties.description: DB connection config. Option A (preferred): {"dbConfig": "sandbox://code/path.cfg"} (must not use jndiName - JNDI is not supported). Option B (inline): {"jdbcSpecific": "POSTGRE", "dbURL": "jdbc:postgresql://hostname/dbname", "user": "u", "password": "p"}. jdbcSpecific is the JDBC driver type — NOT the database name (which belongs in dbURL). Supported: POSTGRE, ORACLE, MSSQL, MSSQL2005, MYSQL, DB2, SQLITE, SNOWFLAKE, REDSHIFT, SYBASE, VERTICA, HIVE, INFORMIX, DERBY, EXASOLUTION, FIREBIRD, PERVASIVE, MSACCESSJAVA, GENERIC. When creating a .cfg: set jdbcSpecific=<TYPE> and database=<TYPE> to the same value — EXCEPT MSSQL with Microsoft driver where database=MSSQLSERVER (not MSSQL).
